 Welcome to “Good Morning, Illini Nation,” your daily dose of college basketball news from Illini beat writer and AP Top 25 voter Scott Richey. He’ll offer up insights every morning on Brad Underwood’s team and college basketball at large: 
 Illinois has had at least one player selected in the first round of the last three NBA drafts. Terrence Shannon Jr. got the streak going in 2023, going No. 27 to the Minnesota Timberwolves. Then came Kasparas Jakucionis (No. 20, Miami Heat) and Will Riley (No. 21, Washington Wizards) as back-to-back picks in 2024. Keaton Wagler made it three drafts in a row last June as the No. 5 overall pick to the Los Angeles Clippers.
 That streak of first-round picks is the first of its kind in program history. Accounting for every round of the draft, Illinois hadn't had picks in three consecutive drafts since 1985-87, which included Ken Norman going in the first round in 1987 as the 19th pick to the Clippers.
 Illinois could find itself in even rarer territory come next June. Quentin Coleman doesn't just project to be another first-round pick. The freshman guard could be the second straight one-and-done lottery selection out of Champaign. 
 Just how high Coleman might go was part of the conversation on the latest episode of "The Kevin O'Connor Show" with Yahoo! Sports' draft expert and special guest John Fanta. The NBC play-by-play man was on the call last week for the Illinois-Texas Tech game in Lubbock, Texas.
 "I got a text the middle of last week from a scout I've known a long time," O'Connor said on the podcast. "He said, 'KOC, Underwood did it again. Wagler last year, and Coleman this year. Coleman is going to go top five — maybe even No. 1. Watch his Texas Tech game if you haven't. He makes one of the best defensive plays I've seen this year deflecting away a lob. He got banged up and still had 19 points making passes all over. He's a stud. Do not overlook this kid."

 Scott Richey covers college basketball for The News-Gazette. His email is srichey@news-gazette.com , and you can follow him on Twitter ( @srrichey ).
